main_text.l: Propositio: Hortari te, ne amet has ineptias.

Ratio I. ab inhonesto: Quia hæc κακοζηλία[?] fit index animi variis vitiis corrupti: Enumerentur aliquot vitia: Levitas abjiciens res consuetas sine causa: nec habens studium retinendi famam honestam.
Superbia, efferens se supra alios, & se ostentans.
Stultitia, amans & eligens indecora, & invisa prudentibus.
Lascivia: prodens & irritans pravas animi cupiditates.
Probetur minor authoritate Bernhardi: Vestium curiositas deformitatis mentium & morum indicium est. Et vulgari dicto: vestis virum indicat.
Amplificetur I. ex descriptione κακοζηλίας[?], quod sit prava affectatio ejus, quod est ultra virtutem, judicio carens, & specie boni fallens.
II. a contrario, h. e., a fine vestium, qui est tegumentum turpitudinis.
Ratio II. ab inhonesto: Quia fit aliena a professione tua, quam suscepseris. Probetur ex fine Theologiæ: & ex dictis, Tit.2.7.2.Tim.2.22. Juveniles cupiditates fuge.
Amplificetur a minori: Ethicam requirere auditorem non indulgentem animi perturbationibus & affectibus. Multo magis Theologiam.
1. quod offendere posset oculos sui Principis.

page.notes: The left-margin notes are partly worn. "Lib.3.de con-sideratione" is a best reading of a faint, abbreviated reference, marked as uncertain. The Greek word after "Quia hæc" and in "Amplificetur I." is hard to read at this resolution; the accents and letters are uncertain. The final line "4. quod" is a fragment that continues beyond the page. Some margin notes may be tied to lines slightly differently in print.
